verdict: Confirmed. transport_config (config.rs:79-89) only sets keep-alive, datagram buffers and idle timeout. iroh's builder starts from noq TransportConfig::default(), which gives max_concurrent_bidi_streams 100, max_concurrent_uni_streams 100, stream_receive_window 1.25 MB and receive_window VarInt::MAX, i.e. unlimited (noq-proto config/transport.rs default; iroh quic.rs:150-160 only changes path and NAT settings). noq buffers data for remote-opened streams the app never accepts, up to each stream's window, and the connection-level window is unlimited. Server and DM connections accept exactly one bidi stream, so the other 99 bidi streams (and uni streams wherever no video reader runs) can each be filled with 1.25 MB that stays buffered while keep-alives hold the connection open. accept_incoming (dm.rs:435-456) admits any identity with the right conv id, and any frame resets the 120 s idle timer (dm.rs:468-489), so each throwaway identity can pin about 250 MB. Pre-auth server connections get 4 s and a frame of up to 1 MiB (proto.rs:15-25), with no limit on concurrent handshakes.
refined_fix: (1) Endpoint-wide (the Router gives no per-connection accept_with): set receive_window to about 16 MiB (a hard cap on buffered data per connection regardless of stream count), stream_receive_window to about 1 MiB, max_concurrent_bidi_streams to about 8 (iroh-blobs only needs a few concurrent requests) and max_concurrent_uni_streams to about 16. Benchmark a 25 MB attachment transfer and a screen share at 4.5 Mbps after the change. (2) In Link::spawn for server and DM links, run a loop that accepts further bidi streams and stops/resets them at once (this frees credit and memory). Where no video reader runs, accept uni streams and stop them too. (3) proto.rs: a global semaphore of about 64 for connections waiting for their first frame, at most one pending connection per remote id, and a first-frame size limit of about 256 KiB. (4) See DOS-15 for limiting stranger DM connections.

title: Unlimited sybil joins grow every replica forever and can push SyncHave past MAX_FRAME, after which it is silently dropped and sync stops for everyone
scenario: A member creates an unlimited-use invite (any member may) and joins with thousands of fresh keypairs. Each JoinRequest (mod.rs:835-851) makes the host sign a MemberAdmit and store and fan out it plus the Profile (host.rs:475-493). Every member stores both forever, and members and Heads grow by one author each. At about 31k authors (about 34 B each), Ctl::SyncHave exceeds MAX_FRAME (core wire.rs:17). encode_frame fails and Link::send returns true without sending anything (link.rs:249-254). After that no member can resync or join with history, which diverges honest replicas permanently. Sybils would also supply 'verified' attestations under the S1 fix. Related: a JoinAccepted link sits in h.joiners until it sends Hello (host.rs:130, mod.rs:841, 707-715), with no per-peer limit or timeout, so one invite holder can park unlimited connections. A repeated JoinRequest from an existing member loads every state event from SQLite (host.rs:467-473) on the actor.
fix: Rate-limit admits per invite_pk (for example 5/min) and per InviteCreate author (for example 20/hour), and cap total members (for example 1000; the target is 50) in admit_joiner. Allow one joiner link per peer (replace the old one), close joiners that send no Hello within 10 s, and cap joiners at about 16. Find an existing admit through an index in ConvState instead of state_events. Make Link::send log and return false when encoding fails. Split SyncHave/Heads into chunks so a frame can never exceed MAX_FRAME.
verdict: Confirmed, and cheaper than the scenario says. Heads encodes at about 33 B per author. Past about 31k authors, encode_frame fails with FrameTooLarge (core wire.rs:369-373), and Link::send returns true without sending anything (link.rs:249-254). Every SyncHave from a fully synced replica (member.rs:143 VvDigest resync, host.rs:390/763, the probe at 634) is then silently lost. Fresh joiners (empty heads) still get history, but a replica that misses any live event can never recover, so honest replicas diverge permanently. Sybils do not even need JoinRequests: MemberAdmit has no host-only rule (state.rs:640-644; any member may author it against its own invite), and Ctl::Events from a member is ingested without an author==sender check (host.rs:752 -> mod.rs:1268). So one member can push about 31k MemberAdmit events plus self-signed sybil Profile events (about 12 MB) in one go. Also confirmed: JoinAccepted links sit in h.joiners keyed by link id, with no per-peer limit and no timeout (mod.rs:839-841; removed only on Closed or first frame). A repeated JoinRequest from an existing member runs storage.state_events (every state event) on the actor (host.rs:467-473).
refined_fix: (1) Remove the frame cliff, which is the actual divergence: append a Ctl variant such as `SyncHavePart { heads, more: bool }`. Senders split Heads into chunks of about 512 KiB, and receivers accumulate the parts until more=false before running the existing SyncHave logic. Separate full SyncHave frames cannot be used for this, because each one is treated as a complete view. Make Link::send and CtlTx::send log and return false when encoding fails. (2) Host-side, per link and per UserId (not validation, which must stay order-independent): limit the authors that a member's Publish/Events may introduce (for example at most 20 new authors and 20 MemberAdmit events per minute per link), plus per-invite_pk admit limits in admit_joiner (for example 5/min). (3) Joiners: at most one joiner link per peer (replace the old one), close joiners that send no Hello within 10 s, and cap the joiner total at about 16. (4) Find an existing admit through an index (user -> admit id) in ConvState or storage instead of scanning state_events.

title: Per-member Have set and clip list are unbounded, and every WhoHas scans all clips of all members
scenario: Ctl::Have{add} inserts into m.have with no limit (774-782). A member streams 1 MiB Have frames (about 32k random hashes each), so the host's memory grows about 1.5x the attacker's bytes until OOM. Hello.clips (up to about 30k ClipInfo in 1 MiB) is stored as a Vec (accept_member, 378), and holders() runs `m.clips.iter().any(..)` for every member on every WhoHas (244-258). After a Hello with 30k clips, the attacker sends 40-byte WhoHas frames: about 25k/s x 30k comparisons saturates the session actor, honest Ticks wait behind it, and members are dropped as silent.
fix: Cap m.have (for example 20k entries) and Have.add/remove per frame (for example 1024), closing the link when exceeded. Cap clips at about 256 and put clip hashes in the have HashSet so holders() is O(members). Give WhoHas a per-member bucket of about 20/s.
verdict: Confirmed. Ctl::Have{add} inserts into m.have with no limit (host.rs:774-782). 1 MiB frames of about 32k hashes each grow a HashSet by roughly 1.5-2x the attacker's bytes, for as long as the link lives. Hello.clips (up to about 25-30k ClipInfo in 1 MiB) is stored as a Vec (accept_member, host.rs:377-378). holders() (244-258) runs `m.clips.iter().any(..)` for every member on every WhoHas, so a 37-byte WhoHas costs about 30k 32-byte comparisons on the session actor. At about 25k WhoHas/s (roughly 1 MB/s) that saturates the actor, honest Ticks wait in LINK_QUEUE, and members are dropped as silent after 10 s.
refined_fix: Cap m.have (for example 20k entries) and Have.add/remove per frame (for example 1024); over the cap, ignore the frame or close the link. Cap clips at about 256 and the clip name length (see DOS-03). Put clip hashes into a HashSet (or into `have`) so holders() is O(members). Give WhoHas a per-member token bucket of about 20/s keyed by UserId in HostState.

title: Event signatures are verified on the session actor while holding the replica lock, without a stale pre-check, and all links share one FIFO
scenario: ingest_signed verifies every event (StoredEvent::from_signed) inside `self.replica.lock()` (1270-1289), with no per-link budget, for Events from any member (host.rs:752-756). Publish (host.rs:840-870) also does a SQLite read on Stale. A member sends 1 MiB Events frames full of already-known events or random signatures (about 8k ed25519 verifications, around 250 ms CPU per frame). The actor and the replica lock stall, which also blocks send_missing, SFU is_voice_channel and the app's state reads. All links feed one LINK_QUEUE of 1024 (mod.rs:327, link.rs:225), so honest members' Ticks wait behind the attacker's frames. last_rx is set only when a frame is processed, so the host drops honest members as silent after 10 s. At roughly 30 Mbps the attacker keeps this up continuously.
fix: Before verifying, decode the event and drop it when seq <= head(author): such events are never applied (Stale), so skipping the check is safe. Verify signatures in the link reader task, off the actor and outside the lock, and pass StoredEvents to the actor. Close a member link on its first invalid signature (honest clients never send one). Add a per-link events/s budget, and a per-link in-flight limit (for example a semaphore of 8) so one link cannot monopolise LINK_QUEUE.
verdict: Confirmed. ingest_signed verifies every event with StoredEvent::from_signed (signed.verify()) inside `self.replica.lock()` (mod.rs:1270-1289), before any stale check. Already-known or invalid events cost a full ed25519 verify each, about 7k per 1 MiB frame, roughly 250 ms. The actor and the replica lock stall, which also blocks send_missing tasks, is_voice_channel and the app's reads. All links share one LINK_QUEUE of 1024 (mod.rs:327, 334). Once the attacker sends faster than the actor verifies (about 4 MiB/s), the queue fills with its frames, honest Ticks wait behind them for more than 10 s, and since last_rx is set only when a frame is processed (host.rs:735-737), honest members are dropped as silent. The queue can also hold about 1024 decoded frames of about 1 MiB each, so about 1 GiB of memory.
refined_fix: (1) Before verifying, decode the Event (cheap) and skip it when conv != server or seq <= head(author): such events can only be Stale or equivocations and are never applied. (2) Verify signatures in the link reader task, off the actor and outside the lock, and pass StoredEvents to the actor. (3) Close a member link on its first invalid signature (honest peers only forward events they verified). (4) Per-link in-flight limit (for example a semaphore of 8 frames, or a byte budget of about 4 MiB) so one link cannot fill LINK_QUEUE; this also caps the queue's memory. Optionally add a per-link events/s budget keyed by UserId.

title: Status flapping makes the host broadcast the full roster every 250 ms, and every member rewrites storage
scenario: A member alternates Status fields (muted, voice, uptime, hosting_ok) as fast as it likes. Each Status calls mark_roster (767-772), and the 250 ms debounce (215-219, 967-973) turns that into 4 full Roster broadcasts per second to all N members (about N x 80 B each). With 50 members that is about 800 KB/s (6.4 Mbps) of host upload from a few bytes of input. On every member, note_roster (mod.rs:1323-1349) rewrites the roster kv whenever succession changes (which flipping hosting_ok or synced causes), emits RosterUpdated (UI re-render 4 times a second) and calls dm.peers_seen.
fix: Give Status a per-member bucket (1/s, keep only the latest). Enforce at least 1 s between roster broadcasts, rising to 5 s when there were more than 20 changes in the last minute. Skip the broadcast when the built roster equals the last one sent, ignoring rev.
verdict: Confirmed. Every Ctl::Status calls mark_roster (host.rs:767-772). The 250 ms debounce (ROSTER_DEBOUNCE_MS, host.rs:215-219, 967-973) means a member flipping a field more than 4 times per second gets 4 full Roster broadcasts per second sent to all members. A RosterEntry is about 100-170 B with relay URL and addresses, so with 50 members that is about 7 KB x 49 x 4/s, roughly 1-1.5 MB/s (8-12 Mbps) of host upload from a few bytes of input, enough to saturate a home uplink. Honest status changes are human-paced. On members, note_roster (mod.rs:1323-1349) rewrites the roster kv whenever succession changes (flip hosting_ok or synced), emits RosterUpdated with a cloned roster and calls dm.peers_seen, 4 times a second.
refined_fix: Enforce a global minimum interval between roster broadcasts in HostState (1 s, rising to 5 s after more than 20 changes in the last minute). This also covers reconnect and path-change triggers (DOS-16). Skip the broadcast when the built roster equals the last one sent, ignoring rev. Coalesce Status per member: store the latest, apply it at most once a second, with the state keyed by UserId.

title: A malicious host can poison members' address tables and peers with fake roster entries (unbounded memory and disk writes, cold-open eclipse)
scenario: Any member can become host legitimately. member.rs:111-117 accepts every Roster from the current host, and note_roster calls learn_hint, persist_peer (a SQLite upsert plus the `persisted` map) and dm.peers_seen for every entry, with no membership check. A 1 MiB roster holds about 10k random user ids. Changing their addresses each time means storage writes on every roster, and the hints, MemoryLookup and persisted maps grow without bound. The fake entries carry the newest last_seen, so storage.peers(server, 6) in cold_candidates (1378-1397) returns only fakes; after a restart the member dials 6 fake ids plus the attacker and never reaches honest members, which leaves them partitioned. The decoded roster (about 5x the wire size because of SocketAddr vectors) is also cloned into RosterUpdated, which the 4096-slot event bus can retain. Holders lists (member.rs:148-155) and the roster's succession are also accepted from the host without checks.
fix: In note_roster, skip entries where `!self.is_member(&e.user)`, remove duplicates, and cap entries at the member count. Enforce AddrHint limits at decode (at most 8 direct addresses, relay URL at most 256 B). Persist peers only for members. Keep only member ids in succession. Cap Holders at about 32 member entries.
verdict: Confirmed; a malicious host is in scope because any member can host. member.rs:111-117 accepts any Roster from the current host with r.epoch >= mine. note_roster (mod.rs:1326-1333) calls learn_hint, persist_peer (a SQLite upsert whenever the address differs) and dm.peers_seen for every entry, with no is_member check. A 1 MiB roster holds about 10-20k minimal entries. Changing the addresses each time forces that many upserts per roster, at whatever rate the host sends, and hints, MemoryLookup and `persisted` grow without bound. Peers are read with ORDER BY last_seen_ms DESC LIMIT 6 (store storage_impl.rs:333), so fresh fake entries fill every cold-open slot, and succession (cold_candidates, mod.rs:1383-1386) is also host-controlled. That makes for a strong, if not total, cold-open eclipse (rendezvous and mDNS can still help). learn_hint caps direct addresses at 8, but persist_peer stores the raw AddrHint, and Holders (member.rs:148-155) is passed on without checks.
refined_fix: In note_roster, skip entries where `!self.is_member(&e.user)` (take the replica lock once and filter), remove duplicate users, and cap entries at the member count. Only member ids may go into succession and the persisted roster. Truncate the AddrHint before persisting (at most 8 direct addresses, relay URL at most 256 B), or reject it at decode. Process at most about 4 rosters/s from the host. Cap Holders at about 32 entries and keep only members.

title: Any stranger identity creates a persistent DM conversation and a peer entry, holds a connection open, and can flood typing, call and state events (documented gap)
scenario: A DmHello with the correct conv id from any key passes accept_incoming. open_conv (343-377) upserts a ConvRecord, inserts a Replica and emits DmOpened, and register adds a DmPeer entry that is never removed. An attacker generating keypairs at handshake speed creates millions of conversations in storage, memory and the UI list, with no limit on concurrent DM links (468-489: any frame resets the idle timer). Per link, Typing (531-535) emits a NetEvent per frame. CallInvite then CallEnd in a loop (hub.rs:325-361) rings the UI repeatedly and spawns ring timers. CallState toggles emit CallUpdated per frame. Together these keep the 4096-slot event bus lagging.
fix: Do not persist a conversation on DmHello from a peer who shares no server and is not an existing contact. Keep strangers in an in-memory request list (cap 32, LRU, at most 20 messages each) until the user accepts. Cap concurrent stranger DM links (for example 8) and new stranger connections per minute. Add per-peer buckets: Typing 1 per 2 s, CallInvite 1 per 10 s, CallState 2/s. Remove DmPeer entries that have no conversation, link or hold.
verdict: Confirmed. accept_incoming (dm.rs:435-456) only checks that conv == ConvId::dm(me, peer) and peer != me. open_conv (343-377) then upserts a ConvRecord, inserts a Replica and emits DmOpened for any new key, and register keeps a DmPeer entry. Any frame resets the 120 s idle timer (run_conn, 468-489), and there is no limit on concurrent DM links or new-identity rate. This is reachable by a malicious member, since every member learns every other member's UserId from rosters and events: generating keypairs creates unbounded conversations in storage, in memory and in the UI. Per link, Typing (531-535) emits a NetEvent per frame, CallInvite/CallEnd loops ring the UI and spawn ring timers (hub.rs:325-361), and CallState toggles emit CallUpdated, all with no rate limit.
refined_fix: For a DmHello from a peer who shares no server with me and is not an existing contact (has no stored conv), keep the request in memory (cap 32, LRU, at most about 20 messages each). Persist the conv only when the user accepts or replies. Cap concurrent stranger DM links (for example 8) and new stranger connections per minute (for example 10). Add per-peer buckets: Typing 1 per 2 s, CallInvite 1 per 10 s, CallState 2/s. Remove DmPeer entries that have no conversation, link or hold.

title: One author can fill the global PendingBuffer and evict honest early events
scenario: PendingBuffer is capped at 10k events / 32 MiB per replica, dropping the oldest first (state.rs:97-100). A member sends Events frames with its own validly signed events at seq head+2 and above (Gap), or with hlc more than 5 minutes ahead (Future). The host buffers them through ingest_signed (mod.rs:1283) and so do members through fan-out. Honest out-of-order events in the buffer are evicted and need a later resync (VvDigest every 60 s, or SyncHave, which DOS-02 makes expensive), which delays delivery for everyone.
fix: Give PendingBuffer a per-author quota (for example 256 events or 1 MiB) and evict from the offending author first. On member links, do not buffer Future events at all, and drop Gap events more than 1024 seqs ahead of the author's head.
verdict: Confirmed, and worse than stated. Events from a member are ingested without an author check (host.rs:752 -> mod.rs:1283), and PendingBuffer::ingest buffers Gap and Future verdicts (state.rs:936-939) in one per-replica buffer of 10k events / 32 MiB that evicts the oldest first (873-881). The verdict is Gap not only for seq > head+1 but also for any author who is not a member (state.rs:605-608). So a member can fill the buffer with validly self-signed events from unlimited fresh keypairs, and a per-author quota alone does not stop it. Honest early events are evicted and have to wait for a VvDigest/SyncHave resync. On top of that, drain_ready runs after every Accept and walks every distinct pending author (next_author, drop_stale and lookups, state.rs:900-925). With 10k junk authors buffered, each applied event costs about 1-2 ms, so bulk ingests (merge sync, resync, a malicious host's history) stall the actor long enough for members to be dropped as silent. Live fan-out only forwards applied events, so members are only affected by a malicious host.
refined_fix: (1) In PendingBuffer, give each author a quota (for example 256 events or 1 MiB) and add a small global cap (for example 64 events) for events whose author is not yet a member. Over quota, drop the new event, not the oldest honest one. (2) On links from members, drop Gap events more than 1024 seqs ahead of the author's head, and drop Future events more than an hour ahead instead of buffering them. (3) Make drain_ready revisit only authors that can have become ready (the author just applied, plus authors gated on membership, channel or target when a MemberAdmit, ChannelCreate or Message applied), or cap distinct pending authors so each scan stays bounded.

title: mDNS sightings from any LAN host grow the hints table and MemoryLookup without bound
scenario: Every mDNS Discovered event calls learn_hint for the announced id (net.rs:152-156, inner.rs:212-230) before any membership check (wake only filters later). A non-member on the LAN announcing random endpoint ids makes `hints` and the iroh MemoryLookup grow forever.
fix: Learn mDNS hints only for ids that are a member of one of my servers or a DM contact. Put an LRU cap of about 4096 on `hints`.
verdict: Confirmed, low severity (needs a LAN attacker, no membership needed). In net.rs:147-158, every mDNS Discovered event calls net.learn_hint for the announced id before wake() does any membership filtering. learn_hint (inner.rs:212-230) inserts into `hints` (a HashMap with no cap) and into the iroh MemoryLookup for every new id. merge_hint caps addresses per id at 8, but not the number of ids. A LAN host announcing random endpoint ids under 'tincan1' grows both maps forever.
refined_fix: In the mDNS loop, learn the hint and wake only if the id is a member of one of my servers (any replica's state.is_member) or a DM contact (has a DM conv). Otherwise ignore the sighting. Put an LRU cap of about 4096 entries on `hints`; when evicting, never drop entries for members or contacts.

title: The voice session command channel is unbounded and fed by remote media control frames
scenario: VoiceCmd uses mpsc::unbounded_channel (voice.rs:141). Every media Ctl from the host (hub.rs:270-275) or the call peer (hub.rs:316-318) is pushed as VoiceCmd::FromPeer. If the voice actor runs slower than the session or DM actor (for example while pushing share frames or re-seeding, DOS-06), a flood of KeyframeRequest, Subscribe or SoundPlayed frames grows the queue without bound.
fix: Use a bounded channel (for example 256) for FromPeer and drop with try_send when full. Keep local app commands on a separate bounded channel that waits for space, so they are never dropped.
verdict: Confirmed but contingent and low severity. The voice command channel is mpsc::unbounded_channel (voice.rs:141). Remote frames are pushed into it without a bound: FromPeer from the host (hub.rs:270-275) and from an active call peer (hub.rs:316-318), plus NeedKeyframe from SessionSink::gap (voice.rs:686-689). For the queue to grow, the consumer must be slower than the producer. That holds in a call while I share: each Subscribe or KeyframeRequest does add_remote or viewer_wants_key (spawning a writer and seeding up to 160 frames, tens of microseconds), while the DM actor only decodes and forwards the 5-byte frame in a few microseconds. So a call peer flooding Subscribe grows the queue at hundreds of thousands of entries per second (each entry is a whole Ctl value). In rooms the consumer work per message (request_keyframe with coalescing, emit) is about the producer's, so the queue does not grow there.
refined_fix: Add a separate bounded channel (for example 256) for remote-sourced commands (FromPeer, NeedKeyframe), filled with try_send and dropped when full. Keep the app's local commands (Transport, Share*, Subscribe, Stop, ...) on the existing channel so they are never dropped, and have the actor select both channels, local first. Fixing DOS-06 (early return on a duplicate Subscribe and a re-seed rate limit) removes the slow-consumer case.
